property_summary: After any successful SetLogFile(addr), a subsequent payable Put must succeed because C forwards the log to the configured LogFile; the mutant never stores the address, so LogFile stays address(0) and Put reverts for every input.
After SetLogFile points at a reverting logger, every Put must revert (the forwarded AddMessage fails); the mutant never stores the logger, so Put spuriously succeeds for some inputs.

After SetLogFile(configuredLogger), every deposit via Put must forward its mandatory audit log to that logger; with a logger whose AddMessage reverts, Put must revert in the reference C, but the mutant (never storing the logger, leaving address(0) whose empty code accepts the call) lets Put spuriously succeed for some (actor, amount, lockTime).

Once a log contract is configured via SetLogFile, every successful deposit must be recorded through it; hence a logger that rejects AddMessage forces every Put to revert, leaving c's balance at zero — the mutant never stores the logger (address(0)), so the silent no-op call lets Put succeed and c's balance becomes nonzero for some fuzzed (actor, amount).

After SetLogFile(log), any subsequent Put by a caller must succeed because LogFile points to the given log address; the mutant stores msg.sender instead, so a contract caller with no AddMessage function makes Put revert for some inputs.

For any log address and any deposit amount, after SetLogFile(logAddr) a subsequent Put must succeed because LogFile points to the given (codeless) address whose AddMessage call trivially succeeds; the mutant stores address(this) as LogFile, so Put's LogFile.AddMessage call reverts for many inputs.

After SetLogFile(log) is called by a contract caller H, any later Put by H must still succeed because LogFile points to the supplied log contract; the mutant stores H itself as LogFile, so Put's LogFile.AddMessage call reverts for some deposit amounts.
